## Recommendation: sql.js (not sqlite-wasm, not wa-sqlite/OPFS)

**Verdict:** Use [`sql.js`](https://github.com/sql-js/sql.js/) (v1.14.1, healthy: 13.6k stars, 646k weekly downloads, released ~3 months ago) to load a pre-built, read-only `.sqlite` file entirely in memory in the browser. Skip `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` and `wa-sqlite` — both exist primarily to support **persistent, writable, cross-origin-isolated OPFS storage**, which this project doesn't need (your data is read-only and rebuilt at build time, not mutated client-side). Pulling in OPFS support only buys you COOP/COEP header requirements (`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` + `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`) that are awkward to set reliably through a Vercel multi-zone rewrite and buy nothing for a read-only workload. ([sqlite.org/wasm/doc/trunk/persistence.md](https://sqlite.org/wasm/doc/trunk/persistence.md), [powersync.com blog](https://powersync.com/blog/sqlite-persistence-on-the-web))

**Why sql.js fits your constraints exactly:**
- No SharedArrayBuffer, no special headers, no Worker requirement — it just `fetch()`s the wasm binary and the `.sqlite` file as ArrayBuffers and queries in memory. Works on any static host, including Vercel's basePath multi-zone setup, with zero header config.
- Bundle cost: ~640KB `sql-wasm.wasm` raw (~320KB gzip) + ~40KB JS glue. Load it lazily via `dynamic import()` on first data-view mount, not in the initial JS bundle.
- Growth path: at "country-wide metrics" scale, if the whole DB gets too big to ship eagerly, layer [`sql.js-httpvfs`](https://github.com/phiresky/sql.js-httpvfs) on top — it's the same sql.js/wasm core plus an HTTP Range-request VFS, so only the needed DB pages are fetched. Works on any static host since range requests are standard HTTP (GitHub Pages, Vercel static assets). Caveat: last npm publish ~2022, effectively unmaintained, but it's thin enough over sql.js that risk is low. Not needed yet at 168-city scale.

**next.config.ts changes: ideally none.** Next.js 16 makes Turbopack the default for both `dev` and `build`, and Turbopack currently has a known gap importing `.wasm` via ES `import`/`require` ([vercel/next.js#84972](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/84972)) — while webpack's `asset/resource` rule workaround exists, adding a custom `webpack()` block to `next.config.ts` will actually **fail** a Turbopack-default build unless you also pass `--turbopack` explicitly ([nextjs.org/blog/next-16](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)). Sidestep this entirely: don't `import` the `.wasm`. Put `sql-wasm.wasm` and your compiled `data.sqlite` in `public/`, and use sql.js's `locateFile` callback to `fetch` them at runtime with the basePath prefix (same pattern you already use for other static assets under `/mapstack`), e.g. `initSqlJs({ locateFile: f => \`${basePath}/${f}\` })`. No bundler config touches `.wasm` at all.

**Build-time `.sqlite` generation:** Given the project already mixes Python (`scripts/gen_crime_data.py`) and Node, add a small Node prebuild script using **`better-sqlite3`** (sync API, zero-fuss, well-tested) to compile the existing generated JSON into a `.sqlite` file before `next build`. Alternative: Node 22+'s built-in `node:sqlite` avoids an extra dependency, but it's still only RC-stable as of Node 24 (fully stable at Node 26) and lacks a `db.transaction()` helper and buffer serialize/deserialize ergonomics — verify Vercel's build image Node version before committing to it. `better-sqlite3` is the safer default.

**Playwright:** No gotchas. Since sql.js needs no SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin-isolation/Worker, it runs fine in Playwright's default headless Chromium context against `pnpm build && pnpm start` with no extra config — unlike OPFS-based libraries, which would need a cross-origin-isolated test context.

Sources: [sql.js GitHub](https://github.com/sql-js/sql.js/), [npm sql.js](https://www.npmjs.com/package/sql.js), [sqlite.org/wasm persistence docs](https://sqlite.org/wasm/doc/trunk/persistence.md), [PowerSync SQLite-on-web 2026 update](https://powersync.com/blog/sqlite-persistence-on-the-web), [sql.js-httpvfs](https://github.com/phiresky/sql.js-httpvfs), [Next.js 16 blog](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16), [next.js#84972 Turbopack wasm](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/84972), [Node.js sqlite docs](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.13.1/docs/api/sqlite.html).
